I’ll first read the workspace contract, then apply the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake dogfish target policy. I’ll inspect rollout keyframes and inherited evidence before touching `solver/`, and I’ll keep the candidate and both required evidence files in lockstep.

The workspace has four sampled solver results: two duplicate high scorers and two duplicate lower scorers, all reaching the target. I’m narrowing the evidence set to unique policies and will use inherited optimizer logs to supply the required failure comparison, rather than treating duplicate evaluations as independent support.

The inherited logs show the useful one-axis sequence: fraction `0.40` captured at `39.710`, shifting anteriorly to `0.45` regressed to `43.323` with higher distance, crossflow, loads, energy, and joint excursions, while shifting posteriorly to `0.35` improved arrival to `38.362` and mean distance to `1.812L`. Per the visual-signal skill, I’m now checking the common prewarm sheet and the released `0.35`/`0.45` sheets before selecting the next axis.

The skill-driven visual comparison confirms the metric story: both policies actively self-propel and enter the same wake corridor, but `0.35` completes the early turn and diagonal traverse sooner; `0.45` spends longer on the turn/approach and shows a broader disturbed trail before capture. I’ll record that diagnosis now, before changing the candidate, and test only the next bounded distribution step (`0.35 → 0.30`) while keeping the successful gait, gain, and signal set fixed.

The candidate is now a single-parameter `0.30` allocation test, and the durable guidance records the full `0.45 → 0.40 → 0.35` evidence chain plus its load tradeoff and falsification boundary. The visual-signal skill materially constrained the change: no new observation or gait term was added because the released sheets support allocation as the clean axis.
